title: CLO5.1 New Features Live Broadcast Replay 20191021
description: CLO5.1 New Features Live Broadcast Replay 2019-10-21
transcript:
Let's open the CLOAD interface, and first enter the module drawing.  
In the module drawing, we have newly added a folding shirt module.  
Previously, the folding shirt used a fixed front and a folded back, which was more time-consuming.  
Now, we have added two types: one is circular, and the other is triangular.  
We will use the circular type as an example.  
You can see there are five shapes here, and there are two types of front clothes.  
The main difference between the front and back clothes is the fold.  
The main difference between the sleeves is the number of folds.  
There are also two types of sleeves: circular and rectangular.  
Additionally, there is a collar.  
First, let's load the collar.  
Then, let's load the front clothes.  
Next, let's load the back clothes.  
The loading process is a bit slow.  
Now, let's add a sleeve.  
Then, let's add a sleeve cuff.  
And add another sleeve cuff.  
Finally, let's add the pocket.  
Regarding the tie, you can add it if needed; if not, you don't have to.  
Now you can see this shirt is folded.  
Next, let's go to the physical window to view the fabric.  
We can see this fabric has no texture.  
If texture is needed, you can add it according to your requirements.  
Let's click on the fabric details.  
The difference between these details and the previous version is that it increases the bending strength and deformation force on the corner lines.  
This is mainly an optimization of the fabric.  
As you know, in the previous version, Printed Out could only be done when clothes had texture.  
Now, although this shirt has no texture, it can still be Printed Out.  
Here, we can change the different fabrics to observe the simple material status.  
As I mentioned, our fabric has increased the bending strength and deformation force of the corner lines.  
Let's open the fabric calculation mode.  
As you can see, in the previous version, we had to enter measured data step by step.  
Now, we can enter all data at once.  
We can jump to this interface and input the measured data in one go.  
This is an optimization of the fabric calculation mode.  
Now, let's return to simulation mode.  
Let's take a look at the library window.  
In the previous version, besides Fibrous, there was a blue download button.  
In Hardware and Trace, there was also a blue download button.  
Now, in addition to these two, there are also blue download buttons on Apert and Fibrous.  
Previously, we had to click the Fibrous download button for one-click download.  
Now, we can download each individually according to our needs.  
For example, we click on Apert.  
We can see a single download button in Apert.  
Click to download.  
This download takes some time.  
Let's wait a moment.  
Now the download is complete.  
Other libraries function the same way.  
Each with a blue button has new content available for download.  
You can download according to your needs.  
In the model section, two male and two female models have been added.  
Among the female models, Feifei and Grace were added.  
Among the male models, Henry and Nate were added.  
The male model added Henry and Nate.  
In this model, the female model added Andy and the male model added Henry.  
The male model added Andy and the female model added Danny.  
Now, open Feifei.  
After opening Feifei, we can see a size folder within.  
This is different from previous models.  
In this size folder, there is data from the American Experimental Materials Association.  
There are three main categories.  
The first is Miffy, a female with a more delicate figure.  
Potatoe is a female with a slightly shorter figure.  
Glass is a female with a fuller figure.  
The difference between Curvy and Stripe is that Curvy is considered more attractive than Stripe.  
In the class, we can see the model becomes fuller by applying a single size.  
The male model is similar.  
In the male model, there is an app called Modular Configurator.  
It mainly covers the main models during modeling.  
Because every time the version updates, model sizes change, affecting modeling usage.  
So from version 5.1, special models for the Modular Configurator are provided.  
These models cannot change size; they can only use hair, shoes, posture, and movements.  
Let's look at the first model.  
You can see the motion is "back to the stage."  
But this motion is only for Emma and Kelly.  
In the male model, it is the same, only for Daryl and Martin.  
The male model has undergone major changes.  
During development, we only had two models for the Modular Configurator.  
Previously, models had no gender.  
Now, there is no gender for models over 7 years old, and none for models under 7 years old.  
Since our data library covers ages 8 to 16, for the Modular Configurator, we recommend 8 to 12 years old as the most accurate range.  
Why is there a range of 7 to 20 years old?  
This is because we extended the age range from 8 to 16 years as a reference.  
If your age corresponds to an unrecognized model but your body shape is adult, we recommend using an adult model for conversion.  
Next, let's edit the model in the computer editor.  
Let's increase its height a bit.  
You can see a height size marker appears in 3D when you change height.  
After that, let's make a change to the model.  
Previously, when changing posture, absolute symmetry was not possible—only visual inspection.  
Now, there is a small icon on top of the locator.  
Click it to enable symmetrical posture editing when editing the model posture.  
Next, let's look at some changes in the first model.  
Previously, it was not divided into adult and child models.  
Now, it is divided into adult and child models, which are two different models.  
In the fabric section, six types of hair fabrics have been added.  
These include Anglaise wool, fox wool, water-colored leather, fur-colored wool, etc.  
Additionally, some wool-coated fabrics have been added.  
Their difference lies mainly in weight.  
Some changes are visible in the right-hand logo view.  
Some hair fabrics have been added separately.  
When selecting fabric in preview, if you do not want to use automatically generated hair fabrics, you can use the normal map to find hair fabrics.  
In headwear and trims, the washing texture has been moved there.  
In this ribbon, which is the fox's head, an additional part has been added.  
(In the original text, this sentence was repeated multiple times; here it is stated once.)  
In the walkthrough process, we often need stages to match.  
As you can see, there are four different stage objects in this stage to choose from.  
Next, we will detail the new features updated by making a new outfit.  
First, add a model.  
Then import the DXF file.  
Now, import the DXF file.  
There is no decoding on the model side.  
We can use the tool to compare panel lengths.  
We compare the distance between two panels from sleeve to waistline.  
When reaching the waistline, right-click.  
There are three options:  
1. Length of panel—the decoding is added on the back of the rolling panel.  
2. Fixed panel on the unmoved panel.  
3. Fixed panel on the front panel.  
The two panels can be on both sides.  
We select two panels here.  
After selecting, click return to complete.  
Now, both front and back panels have decoding added.  
Currently, the panel is only half; we want to match the other half.  
Naturally, we think of symmetrical panels and sewing lines.  
There is a new function similar to symmetrical panels and sewing lines called symmetrical.  
Open the sewing line.  
Right-click on the panel.  
We can see the panel opens with symmetrical effect.  
Change the sewing line position, and both sides change simultaneously.  
We can use the panel line expansion tool to change panel length, but previously only to lengthen.  
Now, we can also shrink inward.  
For example, shrink one centimeter inward here.  
We can also lengthen by one centimeter.  
After changing the panel, we usually want to measure corresponding parts, such as chest and waist sizes.  
Here, we use the measurement tool, different from before.  
We use the drawing tool to complete it.  
Click start and double-click to end.  
We can see the size.  
Enter its name in the windowance box on the right.  
Although there is empty space in the center, the panel length is not dense.  
Next, measure the waist length.  
After measurement, we make a simple arrangement for the board.  
Arrange the back piece.  
After arrangement, seal it.  
Since the board is symmetrical, only one side needs to be done.  
Select the free seam line.  
The seam line is simple, with a blue point in the 2D seam line.  
Now, there is also a blue point in the 3D seam line.  
After sewing, we proceed.  
Before simulation, let's discuss differences between simulations.  
This is not a new feature but important to emphasize as many ask during tech support.  
There are four types:  
1. GPU simulation—newly added in versions 5.0 and 5.1. When downloading the new version, the GPU simulation driver needs updating. GPU simulation is fast but less accurate for material simulation.  
2. Ordinary simulation—the most commonly used.

Simulate this cloth.

Increase model height.

The model inflates accordingly.  
Now there is an automatic numbering tool.

If there is a sticker on your board, the sticker size is maintained.  
If you number the board, the sticker will not be numbered; if not, the sticker will be numbered.  
It is known that in the cloud, lower particle diameter slows simulation.  
The same applies to automatic numbering—the lower the particle diameter, the slower the numbering.  
I recommend setting particle diameter to 20 for fastest numbering.  
Click here to see the effect.  
You can see numbering is now set.  
In 2D, there is a reference line in the previous library version.  
Click here to see the reference line.  
Now, let's add fabric to this cloth.  
Click the Music Cartoon tab.  
Click to add texture multiple times.  
Let's separate the front pattern and choose a different pattern.  
Usually, we hide the model in 3D to see the pattern on the back.  
Previously, we couldn't see the back pattern on the second-party interface.  
Now, we can see the back pattern.  
Let's change the back color.  
There is a Palette Library mainly used to add Pantone colors.  
There is a plus sign behind this 1, but it matches the background color and is not visible.  
Click here to see the Pantone color library.  
Because there are many Pantone colors, they are divided into several groups.  
Each group is divided individually.  
We can choose the Pantone color needed to import.  
Let's change the back color to a Pantone color.  
In version 5.1, only the normal map displays.

Save the material in preview.  
When saving, it creates a preview image.

Choose the pattern here.  
Click to confirm and save.

Save it in this folder.

Because this clothing has two colors, choose to maintain single pattern coordinates.

This clothing has two colors.

Save the absolute pattern in the file path.

If not deleted, pattern remains.

Look: only one OBJ file with multiple MTL files.

Enter values as needed.

chunks.content: ## Folding Shirt Module in CLO 5.1 This section explains the new folding shirt module added in CLO 5.1, detailing types of folds, garment components, and fabric handling improvements. The folding shirt module now supports two fold types: circular and triangular, replacing the previous fixed-front and folded-back design, which was more time-consuming. The circular type is used as the example. ### Shirt Components and Fold Types - **Front Clothes:** Two types differing mainly in fold style. - **Back Clothes:** Differ from front in fold structure. - **Sleeves:** Two types—circular and rectangular; differ by the number of folds. - **Collar, Sleeve Cuffs, Pocket, and Optional Tie:** Each component can be loaded and added individually. ### Fabric and Physical Properties - The fabric window shows fabric without texture by default but allows adding texture as needed. - Fabric details now include increased bending strength and deformation force on corner lines, optimizing fabric simulation. - Unlike earlier versions where Printed Out required textured fabrics, now non-textured fabrics can be Printed Out. - Fabric calculation mode is enhanced: measured data can be input all at once instead of step-by-step, streamlining the process. --- ## Library and Model Updates This section covers updates to the CLO 5.1 library system, model additions, size categorizations, and the Modular Configurator tool for model management. ### Library Download System - Blue download buttons are now available for multiple libraries (Fibrous, Hardware, Trace, Apert), enabling selective downloads rather than one-click all. - Downloading a library module can take some time but is straightforward. ### New Models Added - **Female Models:** Feifei, Grace, Andy, Danny. - **Male Models:** Henry, Nate, Andy. - Models now include size folders containing data from the American Experimental Materials Association. ### Size Categories in Models - Female size categories include Miffy (delicate figure), Potatoe (shorter figure), and Glass (fuller figure). - Curvy models are considered more attractive than Stripe. - Male models similarly categorized. - The Modular Configurator provides special models with fixed sizes (non-resizable), allowing changes only to hair, shoes, posture, and movements. - Recommended age range for Modular Configurator models is 8 to 12 years old, covering ages 7 to 20 for reference. - Adult body shapes outside the age range should use adult models. --- ## Model Editing and Symmetry Features This section focuses on model editing capabilities in CLO 5.1, including height adjustment, symmetrical posture editing, and division between adult and child models. - Height adjustment shows a size marker in 3D during editing. - Symmetrical posture editing is enabled via a new icon on the locator, allowing precise symmetrical changes to model posture. - Models are now divided into adult and child categories, treated as separate models, improving accuracy in fittings and simulations. --- ## Fabric and Hair Fabric Enhancements This section details new fabric types, hair fabric additions, and handling of textures, normal maps, and preview features. - Six new hair fabric types added, including Anglaise wool, fox wool, water-colored leather, and various wool-coated fabrics with differences mainly in weight.

chunks.content: - Symmetrical posture editing is enabled via a new icon on the locator, allowing precise symmetrical changes to model posture. - Models are now divided into adult and child categories, treated as separate models, improving accuracy in fittings and simulations. --- ## Fabric and Hair Fabric Enhancements This section details new fabric types, hair fabric additions, and handling of textures, normal maps, and preview features. - Six new hair fabric types added, including Anglaise wool, fox wool, water-colored leather, and various wool-coated fabrics with differences mainly in weight. - Hair fabrics can be selected via normal maps if automatic hair fabric generation is not desired. - Washing textures have been moved to the headwear and trims section. - Additional parts added to some accessories (e.g., fox head ribbon). - Fabric preview supports multiple textures; the back pattern in 3D preview can now be viewed, which was not possible before. - Palette Library includes Pantone colors divided into groups for easy selection and import. - Normal map display is supported in version 5.1 for material previews. - Saved material previews generate preview images for later reference. --- ## New Outfit Creation and Panel Editing Explains procedures for creating new outfits, importing DXF files, panel length comparison, symmetrical editing, and panel length adjustments. - Import DXF files without decoding on the model side. - Use a tool to compare panel lengths between sleeve and waistline. - Three options for decoding panels: 1. Length of panel with decoding added at back of rolling panel. 2. Fixed panel on unmoved panel. 3. Fixed panel on front panel. - Symmetrical editing allows sewing lines and panel edges to update simultaneously. - Panel length can now be both lengthened and shrunk using the panel line expansion tool. - Measurement tool uses a drawing method: click start, double-click to end, then input the measurement name. - Panels can be arranged and sealed; for symmetrical boards, only one side needs arrangement. - Seam lines are visualized with blue points in both 2D and 3D views. --- ## Simulation Types and Settings Describes the four simulation types in CLO 5.1, their purposes, and visual indicators. 1. **GPU Simulation:** Added in versions 5.0 and 5.1. Requires updated GPU driver; faster but less accurate for material simulation. 2. **Ordinary Simulation:** Most commonly used, balanced speed and accuracy. 3. **Completion Simulation:** Used during sewing to simulate fabric conflicts and prevent penetration. 4. **Secret Simulation:** Most precise fabric continuity display, used after fabric quality improvements. Simulation icons: - Secret: red icon with arrow at bottom. - Completion: red icon without arrow. - Ordinary: blue icon. - GPU: empty simulation icon with arrow and star. --- ## Model Resizing and Automatic Numbering Covers resizing virtual models and automatic numbering of panels while preserving design details. - Increasing model height shows the height value in the menu, and model inflates accordingly. - Automatic numbering tool adjusts panel numbering based on model body shape while maintaining panel curve and sticker size.

chunks.content: Simulation icons: - Secret: red icon with arrow at bottom. - Completion: red icon without arrow. - Ordinary: blue icon. - GPU: empty simulation icon with arrow and star. --- ## Model Resizing and Automatic Numbering Covers resizing virtual models and automatic numbering of panels while preserving design details. - Increasing model height shows the height value in the menu, and model inflates accordingly. - Automatic numbering tool adjusts panel numbering based on model body shape while maintaining panel curve and sticker size. - Stickers are excluded from numbering if present; otherwise, stickers are numbered. - Lower particle diameter slows simulation and numbering; recommended particle diameter is 20 for fastest performance. --- ## Fabric Texture and Color Management Details fabric pattern assignment, color changes, and Pantone color library usage. - Multiple textures can be added to fabric via the Music Cartoon tab. - Front and back patterns can be assigned different textures and colors. - Model can be hidden in 3D to better observe patterns. - Back pattern visibility in 3D preview is a new feature. - Pantone colors are accessible via a library divided into groups; colors can be imported and applied. - Normal maps can be added to materials in preview for enhanced realism. - Saved preview images help verify fabric appearance. --- ## Virtual Model Pose and Rotation Sets Describes pose editing and rotation set creation for virtual models. - Model pose can be changed. - Rotation sets are created and controlled by a specific button. - Confirmation steps ensure no unintended changes occur to pose or rotation during editing. --- ## Particle Diameter and Selection Function Explains particle diameter impact on simulation and new selection function to optimize performance. - Lower particle diameter improves simulation detail but reduces speed. - Selection function allows reducing particle diameter selectively by choosing only the external lines of the board. - Setting particle diameter to 1 for selected edges improves performance without affecting entire panel. --- ## Foldable Axis and Texture Customization Details the addition of free foldable axes and customization options for fold lines. - New free foldable axis type can be added besides existing line foldable axes. - Textures can be assigned to foldable axes to represent them visually. - Width and color of foldable axes can be adjusted, allowing varied fold line appearances. --- ## Sticker and Illusion Picture Features Explains improvements in sticker rendering using illusion pictures and related properties. - Illusion pictures simulate thickness without physical plates, enhancing rendering realism. - Illusion pictures only visible in rendering, not in 3D interface. - Bulge degree corresponds to grayscale: whiter areas have more pronounced bulge. - Properties include: - **Degree:** Controls bulge intensity. - **Distance:** How far the bulge floats from the panel. - **Picking Up:** Minimum size for bulge display; smaller parts can be hidden. - **Maintain Continuous:** Applies to OBJ files; removes dividing lines for better drag functionality. --- ## Rendering Interface and Fabric Switching Describes rendering interface improvements and fabric material switching.

Requires updated GPU driver; faster but less accurate for material simulation. 2. **Ordinary Simulation:** Most commonly used, balanced speed and accuracy. 3. **Completion Simulation:** Used during sewing to simulate fabric conflicts and prevent penetration. 4. **Secret Simulation:** Most precise fabric continuity display, used after fabric quality improvements. colors can be imported and applied. - Normal maps can be added to materials in preview for enhanced realism. - Saved preview images help verify fabric appearance. --- ## Virtual Model Pose and Rotation Sets Describes pose editing and rotation set creation for virtual models. - Model pose can be changed. - Rotation sets are created and controlled by a specific button. - Confirmation steps ensure no unintended changes occur to pose or rotation during editing. --- ## Particle Diameter and Selection Function Explains particle diameter impact on simulation and new selection function to optimize performance. - Lower particle diameter improves simulation detail but reduces speed. - Selection function allows reducing particle diameter selectively by choosing only the external lines of the board. - Setting particle diameter to 1 for selected edges improves performance without affecting entire panel. --- ## Foldable Axis and Texture Customization Details the addition of free foldable axes and customization options for fold lines. - New free foldable axis type can be added besides existing line foldable axes. - Textures can be assigned to foldable axes to represent them visually. - Width and color of foldable axes can be adjusted, allowing varied fold line appearances. --- ## Sticker and Illusion Picture Features Explains improvements in sticker rendering using illusion pictures and related properties. - Illusion pictures simulate thickness without physical plates, enhancing rendering realism. - Illusion pictures only visible in rendering, not in 3D interface. - Bulge degree corresponds to grayscale: whiter areas have more pronounced bulge. - Properties include: - **Degree:** Controls bulge intensity. - **Distance:** How far the bulge floats from the panel. - **Picking Up:** Minimum size for bulge display;
